newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar eases vs yen in Tokyo after Barshefsky.
newsitem.headline: Dollar eases vs yen in Tokyo after Barshefsky.

text.p: *Dollar eased slightly against yen in early Tokyo trade partly due to comments by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky that U.S. automotive trade deficit with Japan is getting worse and that Tokyo has fallen short of fulfilling agreement to open its market.
*Profit-taking weighed on dollar after it failed to break above 200-day moving average of 117.97 yen overnight, which is widely seen as key resistance point.
*Talk of sales of dollars for yen by Asian central banks.

*"The dollar slipped a bit after Barshefsky's remarks. Some people see the area near the 200-day moving average for dollar/yen as a good level to lock in profits for now," said a trader at a city bank.
*"There is no question that Japan has stalled on deregulation in (the auto) sector. That is of significant concern and inexcusable," Barshefsky told Reuters in an interview on Monday.
*Traders said dollar upside looks heavy near 118 yen, but downside likely to be limited by buying interest from Japanese trust banks and importers.
*"Institutional investors are said to be keen to buy dollars at the lows to unwind hedge dollar sales," said a trader at another city bank.
*Talk circulated of stop-loss dollar buy orders around 118.10 yen, but dollar offers seen heavy around 117.90 yen.
*Dollar also eased against mark on profit-taking in early Tokyo. It rose as high as 1.8490 marks in New York on Monday, its highest level since trading at 1.8690 in November 1989.
*"Dollar/mark may see a correction. People are becoming more cautious about possible action by the Bundesbank," said a trader at another city bank.
